paragraphs.source_en: Not only the master, but even Meitei, who was never startled by anything, seemed quite taken aback by this sudden attack; for a long while he sat there blankly, looking just like a malaria patient suddenly seized with fever. But once their astonishment had passed and they had recovered their usual selves, the comic side of it seized them all at once, and the two burst out laughing together, while Nose alone seemed somewhat disappointed by the turn of events. She glared fiercely at them, thinking it extremely rude to laugh so uproariously at such a moment. Meitei spoke first: “So that is your daughter? Well, this is splendid. You are quite right. See here, Kushami, Kangetsu is certainly in love with this young lady. There is no use hiding it any longer; let us confess everything.” The master merely snorted through his nose and said nothing at all. Nose, triumphant again, said, “Exactly. There is no use hiding it; the whole trick is exposed, isn’t it?” Meitei replied, “If that is how matters stand, there is nothing for it. Anything at all concerning Kangetsu shall be stated for your reference. See here, Kushami, you are the host; nothing will be settled if you merely sit there grinning. Truly, secrets are frightening things. However carefully one keeps them, they leak out somehow. Still, strange is the word for it. Mrs. Kaneda, how did you discover this secret? It is quite astonishing.” Meitei went on chattering all by himself. Asked this, Nose said with self-satisfaction, “There are no gaps on my side either, you know.” Meitei said, “If anything, you have rather too few gaps. Where on earth did you hear it?” “From the wife of the rickshaw man just behind your house.” The master opened his eyes wide and said, “The rickshaw man’s house with the big black cat?” “Yes. As for Mr. Kangetsu, I gave her plenty of instructions long ago. Whenever Mr. Kangetsu comes here, I have the rickshaw man’s wife tell me what he has said.” The master raised his voice and said, “That is outrageous!” “But I do not care in the least what you say or do. I only have her report Mr. Kangetsu’s words.” “Whether it is Kangetsu’s business or anyone else’s, at any rate I detest that rickshaw man’s wife.” The master flew into a rage all by himself. Nose, without blushing in the least, said, “But surely it is her freedom to come and stand by the fence of your house? If you are afraid of being overheard, either lower your voice or move into a larger house. And it is not only the rickshaw man’s household. I have heard all sorts of things from the lady teacher of the two-stringed koto in the new lane as well.” “Things about Kangetsu?” asked the master. Nose spoke in a rather inhuman tone: “Not only about Mr. Kangetsu.” I thought the master would surely admit defeat this time, but to my surprise he said, “That female teacher is always putting on refined airs, acting as though she alone has a proper human face. What a damned fool!” “Begging your pardon, she is a woman. ‘Fellow’ is quite the wrong door to knock on.”

paragraphs.source_zh: 主人不必说了，就连对任何事物从不吃惊的迷亭，对于这突然的袭击，也似乎大吃一惊，好半天呆呆地坐在那里，活像一个突然发起烧来的疟疾病人。但当他们惊愕之情一过，恢复原来面目的时候，那种滑稽的感觉一下子抓住了他们，两个人不约而同地哈哈大笑起来，唯独鼻子稍微感到有些出乎意外。她狠狠地瞪着他们，认为在这种时候狂笑是十分不礼貌的。迷亭首先开口说：“那就是令爱呀？嗯，这太妙啦。您说的一点也不错。喂，苦沙弥君，寒月的确是爱着这位小姐哩。咱们也不用瞒着啦，还是全部都交代出来吧。”主人只用鼻子哼了一声，根本不言语。鼻子又得意地说道：“可不是，你也不用瞒着啦，马脚都露出来啦，是不是？”迷亭答道：“既然这样，还有什么说的，凡有关寒月的事儿，不管什么，都说出来供你参考吧。喂，苦沙弥君，你是主人，一味嘻嘻地笑能解决什么问题呢。说真的，秘密这种东西，真是怪怕人的，不管怎样严加保密，总会泄漏的。不过，要说怪也真够怪的啦，金田太太，你是怎样知道这个秘密的？真想不到啊。”迷亭独自讲个没完。鼻子被这一问，自鸣得意地说道：“我这边也不会有漏洞的呀。”迷亭道：“你可是没有漏洞到过火啦。你到底是从哪儿听说的？”“我是听你们房后的人力车夫老婆说的。”主人睁大眼睛说：“就是养大黑猫的车夫家？”“不错，有关寒月先生的事我早就吩咐过啦，只要寒月先生一来这里，我就让车夫的老婆告诉我，他在这里说了些什么。”主人抬高了声音说道：“这太不像话了！”“不过，你们说些什么我一概不管，我只让她报告寒月先生的话。”“寒月的话也好，谁的也好，反正我讨厌那个人力车夫的老婆。”主人独自在生气。鼻子毫不脸红地说：“不过，到你家墙根下站着，不是人家的自由吗？如果你怕别人听，要么你放低声音，要么你搬到更大的房子去住。不只是拉人力车的，我还从新胡同教二弦琴的女师傅那里听了好多事情呢。”“听了有关寒月的事？”主人问。鼻子说得不像人话：“不仅仅是寒月先生的事。”我以为主人这次可要甘拜下风啦，可是没想到主人竟然说道：“那个女师傅平常似乎像个人儿似的，装得很高尚。真是个王八蛋！”“对不起，人家是个女的，骂王八蛋骂错门啦。”

paragraphs.source_en: The tone of Nose’s speech increasingly revealed what sort of person she was. It was as though she had come here expressly to quarrel. Yet in this respect Meitei was Meitei after all: he did not lose his temper in the slightest, but listened to the two of them crossing swords with lively interest. His manner was like the immortal Li Tieguai enjoying the sight of fighting gamecocks, as he listened on with perfect unconcern.

paragraphs.source_zh: 鼻子说话的语气越来越显露出她是个什么货色。她简直就像是为吵架而来的。可是在这点上，迷亭毕竟是迷亭，他不但毫不动火，反而饶有兴趣地听着这两个人的唇枪舌剑。那神态就好像李铁拐仙人正在欣赏厮打的斗鸡场面一样，抱着无所谓的态度旁听着。
